```{r}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(scales)

m <- read_csv("../data/processed/metrics_latest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Headline numbers
mortgage_rate   <- first(m$mortgage_rate)
rate_date       <- first(m$rate_date)
zillow_date     <- first(m$zillow_date)
median_pay      <- median(m$grad_pay)
median_rent_pct <- median(m$rent_share_solo, na.rm = TRUE)
n_rent_ok       <- sum(m$rent_share_solo <= 0.30, na.rm = TRUE)
median_be       <- median(m$break_even, na.rm = TRUE)
n_never         <- sum(is.na(m$break_even))
median_years    <- median(m$years_to_save)

# Hand the table to the browser-side (OJS) code
ojs_define(metrics = m, mortgage_rate = mortgage_rate)
```

# Renting

## Row {height=22%}

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Typical new-grad pay"
list(value = dollar(median_pay, accuracy = 100), icon = "briefcase", color = "primary")
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Share of pay to rent alone"
list(value = percent(median_rent_pct, accuracy = 1), icon = "house-door",
     color = if (median_rent_pct > 0.30) "danger" else "success")
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Cities where renting alone fits the 30% rule"
list(value = paste(n_rent_ok, "of", nrow(m)), icon = "geo-alt", color = "warning")
```

## Row

### Column {width=28%}

::: {.card title="Use your own salary"}
By default each city uses the **typical full-time pay of a new bachelor's grad there**. Got an offer? Switch to your salary and every city recalculates.

```{ojs}
viewof mode = Inputs.radio(["Typical new-grad pay in each city", "My salary"],
  {value: "Typical new-grad pay in each city"})
viewof my_salary = Inputs.number([10000, 500000],
  {value: 60000, step: 1000, label: "My salary ($/yr)", disabled: mode !== "My salary"})
viewof search = Inputs.search(rows, {placeholder: "Find a city…"})
```

**How to read it:** housing is usually called *affordable* when it takes **30% or less** of gross pay. "With roommate" splits a typical unit's rent in half.
:::

### Column

```{ojs}
//| title: "Rent as a share of pay, 97 largest metros"
rows = transpose(metrics).map(d => {
  const pay = mode === "My salary" ? my_salary : d.grad_pay;
  return {
    City: d.metro,
    Pay: pay,
    "Rent (alone)": d.rent_solo,
    "% of pay (alone)": d.rent_solo * 12 / pay,
    "% of pay (w/ roommate)": d.rent_shared * 12 / pay,
    "Pay needed to rent alone": d.pay_needed_solo,
    Verdict: d.rent_solo * 12 / pay <= 0.30 ? "✅ Fits alone"
           : d.rent_shared * 12 / pay <= 0.30 ? "🟡 Needs a roommate"
           : "🔴 Tight even shared"
  };
})

usd = d3.format("$,.0f")
pct = d3.format(".0%")

Inputs.table(search, {
  sort: "% of pay (alone)",
  rows: 25,
  format: {
    Pay: usd,
    "Rent (alone)": d => usd(d) + "/mo",
    "% of pay (alone)": pct,
    "% of pay (w/ roommate)": pct,
    "Pay needed to rent alone": usd
  }
})
```

## Row

### Column {width=55%}

```{ojs}
//| title: "Break-even mortgage rate vs. today's rate"
owning = transpose(metrics)
  .filter(d => d.break_even !== null)
  .sort((a, b) => b.break_even - a.break_even)

Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 150,
  height: Math.max(400, owning.length * 13),
  x: {label: "Mortgage rate at which a typical new grad could afford a starter home →",
      tickFormat: d => d3.format(".0%")(d), grid: true},
  y: {label: null, domain: owning.map(d => d.metro)},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([mortgage_rate], {stroke: "#d62828", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.text([mortgage_rate], {x: d => d, frameAnchor: "top", dy: -2,
      text: d => `Today: ${d3.format(".2%")(d)}`, fill: "#d62828"}),
    Plot.dot(owning, {x: "break_even", y: "metro",
      fill: d => d.break_even >= mortgage_rate ? "#2a9d8f" : "#e76f51", r: 4,
      tip: true, title: d => `${d.metro}\nBreak-even: ${d3.format(".2%")(d.break_even)}`})
  ]
})
```

### Column

```{ojs}
//| title: "Starter homes: what it takes, by city"
Inputs.table(transpose(metrics).map(d => ({
  City: d.metro,
  "Starter home": d.starter_price,
  "Monthly cost": d.own_cost,
  "% of grad pay": d.own_share,
  "Years to save 10%": d.years_to_save,
  "Break-even rate": d.break_even
})), {
  sort: "Break-even rate",
  reverse: true,
  format: {
    "Starter home": d3.format("$,.0f"),
    "Monthly cost": d => d3.format("$,.0f")(d) + "/mo",
    "% of grad pay": d3.format(".0%"),
    "Years to save 10%": d3.format(".1f"),
    "Break-even rate": d => d === null ? "Never (even at 0%)" : d3.format(".2%")(d)
  }
})
```

# About

::: {.card}
## What this is
**Priced Out** shows recent college grads what it really costs to live in each of America's 97 largest metro areas on an entry-level salary, and whether they could ever buy a home there. It updates as new data is released.

## The signature number: the break-even mortgage rate
For each city, the mortgage rate at which a typical new grad's **total** monthly cost of a starter home (mortgage + property tax + insurance + PMI) equals **30% of their pay**. If it's above today's rate, buying fits the budget now. If it's "never," even a 0% mortgage wouldn't be enough: the problem is price, not rates. This builds on [Zillow's 2025 analysis](https://www.zillow.com/research/rate-drops-35389/), rebuilt live for new grads with 10% down instead of 20%.

## Key assumptions
| Assumption | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| New-grad pay | Metro median earnings of bachelor's holders × 0.79 | ACS 2024 (B20004); ratio from ACS PUMS: full-time grads 22–27 vs all grads 25+ |
| Pay brought to today | × growth in average hourly earnings since 2024 | FRED (CES0500000003) |
| Rent | Typical rent, all units (smoothed, seasonally adjusted) | Zillow ZORI |
| Starter home price | Typical value of the cheapest third of homes | Zillow ZHVI bottom tier |
| Mortgage rate | 30-year fixed, weekly | Freddie Mac via FRED |
| Affordable | Housing ≤ 30% of gross pay | HUD standard |
| Down payment / PMI | 10% down; PMI 0.6% of loan per year | Assumption |
| Property tax | Metro median taxes ÷ median home value | ACS 2024 (B25103, B25077) |
| Insurance | Metro median premium, estimated from brackets | ACS 2024 (B25141) |
| Savings | 10% of pay per year toward a down payment | Assumption |

## Known limitations
- Starter-home prices are compared with **typical** rents (all units), which flatters buying relative to renting.
- New-grad pay assumes young grads earn the same share of the local grad median in every city.
- California property taxes are understated for new buyers (Prop 13); New Orleans insurance is top-coded at $4,000+.
- Utilities and energy costs are not yet included (coming soon).

## Data as of
Mortgage rate: `{r} format(rate_date, "%b %d, %Y")` · Zillow: `{r} format(zillow_date, "%B %Y")` · Census: ACS 2024

*Built by an economics student with AI-assisted development. Code and full decision log on [GitHub](https://github.com/finnmitty725/priced-out). Not financial advice.*
:::
